inline_comments.comment: All three new status values are mapped to `theme.fgColor.accent` here, but `status.tsx` maps them to three different colors: `theme.color.positive` for `new`, `theme.color.secondary` for `modified`, and `theme.color.warning` for `affected`. The two sources of truth disagree, so the sidebar status button renders a different color than the icon returned by `getStatus()` for the same value. The colors in `withStatusColor` should match those in `getStatus` exactly.

`affected` is assigned `theme.color.warning` as its icon color, which is the identical color used by `'status-value:warning'` (a few lines later). The two semantically distinct levels become visually indistinguishable in the sidebar. `affected` ranks *below* `warning` in the priority array, so coloring it the same as `warning` misrepresents the relative severity. Consider a distinct color (e.g., `theme.color.secondary` or `theme.fgColor.accent`) to differentiate it.

The test is named "should rank affected above modified **and below warning**", but this second `expect` asserts that `warning` beats `modified`, not that `warning` beats `affected`. The claim in the test name is therefore unverified. To accurately test the described behavior, the second assertion should use `['status-value:affected', 'status-value:warning']` instead of `['status-value:modified', 'status-value:warning']`.

The `changeDetection` flag is declared with `@default true` in the JSDoc, but no corresponding default is set in `code/core/src/core-server/presets/common-preset.ts`. Per the project rule, opt-out feature flags (those that default to `true`) must have their default set explicitly in the common preset so that standard truthy guards remain correct. Additionally, this flag is not read or used anywhere in this PR — it is dead API surface. The public type should not be added until the implementation that consumes it is ready.

general_comments.comment: The PR description says "Added two new `StatusValue` variants: `status-value:new`, `status-value:modified`" but three values are actually added (`affected` too). The description should be updated to list all three so reviewers and changelog readers are not misled.
